# Daniele Perotti
Builder and Operator · Amsterdam
I help ambitious companies with what they need next: capturing new sources of growth, turning strategy into delivery, and building the leadership team to run it.

## About me
At Rocket Internet I moved to Singapore to launch Zalora's marketplace from zero, then rolled it out across Global Fashion Group. At Booking.com I incubated four new businesses, then led a division of 300+ people with full P&L.
The work I've loved most had three things in common: the energy, the complexity, the learning. Since January 2026 I have worked independently with scale-ups, because that is where I find all three again.
I've been obsessively focused on what AI changes in how a company runs, and the edge it gives the leaders who get there first. All my work runs on my second brain OS and my businesses run on agents I build. Before that, I embedded AI at scale at Booking.com. So I know what holds up in daily operations and what only works in a demo.

### How I lead
I lead by cutting through complexity and holding vision and strategy together. The vision is the big picture and what customers need. The strategy is how we get there: plan, systems, people. This brings to life a culture of energy and engagement, where we create value for the business by creating value for the customer.

### Beyond work
I explore the world through travel, art and music, my constant sources of energy and inspiration. I also care about fitness and wellbeing, especially the ways mindfulness and technology can shape healthier lives.
Building the future starts with making sense of the now.

## Where I come in
For fifteen years I built and ran digital businesses inside the companies that took e-commerce and travel marketplaces to global market leadership. Today I do the same work with scale-ups, beside the founder: new sources of growth, an operating system that scales, and the leaders to run it.
“Making sense of the now” means holding the big picture and the detail that decides it at the same time. That is what turns a founder's vision into clear execution. I operate as a partner and an insider, and what we build together keeps growing long after I've left.

### For founders and CEOs
When every decision still comes to you, when growth has slowed and the fixes tried so far haven't joined up, or when a second business has to be built without starving the first.

### For the funds behind them
When a portfolio company stalls after a round, when a founder needs a leadership team before the next one, or when a company opens a new market or a second line of business.

## Four problems I'm brought in to solve
They are usually connected. Together, we decide where to start and which one to focus on.

### Where to focus, and what to build next
01 · Strategy and transformation
It isn't clear where to focus or what to build next, or a new phase is starting and the team isn't steering by the same number. Often it means a new business built beside the core.
- A clear view of today's business
- Vision, mission and values
- Launching a new line of business
- Strategy, turned into action
- Priorities, and how success is measured

#### A clear view of today's business
What it means: An honest diagnosis before any new plan: which customers, products and markets make the money, where it leaks, how much change the team can really absorb, and what comes first: the risks that threaten the company, then the core business, then new products, then the foundations.
My proof: Booking.com Attractions, taken over during COVID: reassessed, then moved from signing suppliers one by one to partnerships with TUI Musement, Viator and Klook, in seven months. Global Fashion Group: Jabong's operating model moved from just-in-time supply to drop-shipping.

#### Vision, mission and values
What it means: A vision and a North Star the whole company can see, a mission and values people actually use in hiring, onboarding and hard calls, and one company story told the same way to investors, new hires and the team.
My proof: The two businesses I co-own, a Sense of Place, a listening bar and café in Amsterdam, and Masseria Palmita, a boutique hospitality project in Puglia.

#### Launching a new line of business
What it means: A new business built beside the core, using what the core already has (customers, brand, supply, distribution), with the problem and the solution tested before the real money goes in.
My proof: Zalora's marketplace, built from zero in five months beside its retail business, reaching 17.5% of regional net merchandise value by the end of 2015. Booking.com: four new businesses incubated, Flights, Events, Ground Transport and In-stay Services; the hotel extras platform reached €24M revenue and 4.8M transactions. I guide teams through the whole cycle, from idea and validation to first product and launch, with frameworks of my own.

#### Strategy, turned into action
What it means: A three-year plan with its financial model and what needs to be true, broken into 6- and 12-month plans. Every team knows what the strategy asks of it this quarter, and how its work connects to the others'. That means goals and owners per team, progress everyone can see, priorities adjusted as things change, and decisions kept with their reasons.
My proof: Zalora: the marketplace's strategy, operating model and organization defined from scratch. Booking.com: Connected Trip's frameworks became the frameworks the whole product community works with.

#### Priorities, and how success is measured
What it means: Deciding where the effort goes, for example most of it on the core, some on emerging products and a little on future bets, and the few numbers that show whether it is working: one main metric everyone steers by, the early signals beneath it, and a review rhythm that acts on them.
My proof: Booking.com: the company's strongest-ever cross-sell results, with cross-sell volumes up five times. Zalora: the marketplace tracked on delivery time (under 4 days) and seller handling time (under 1.5 days).
> “Working across functions and markets, Dani held the strategic picture and the operational detail at once, building teams obsessed with high standards and high-paced delivery.”
  Alessandro Durì, co-founder of Pemo. We built drop-shipping across Southeast Asia together at Zalora.

### A product customers come back to
02 · Product experience and customer centricity
The product is drifting away from its customers. Competitors move first, customers leave without warning, and product and engineering pull in different directions.
- Knowing the competition
- Customer needs: retention and churn
- The product vision
- The product strategy
- Tech architecture and capabilities

#### Knowing the competition
What it means: A live picture of competitors that product and sales share: what they launch, how they price, where they win, so gaps are found by research rather than by losing deals.
My proof: Rocket Internet: new e-commerce ventures validated against their markets before launch.

#### Customer needs: retention and churn
What it means: Knowing what customers need and why they stay or leave: which customers are at risk before they go, read from usage, service and payment signals, and the experience fixed before they leave.
My proof: Zalora: NPS of 81, out-of-stock cancellations under 1%, and returns kept in line with Zalora's own retail and consignment business, at about 12%.

#### The product vision
What it means: Where the product is going and why, connected to the roadmap, hiring and customer feedback, and updated when the market moves rather than once a year.
My proof: One of three co-owners of Connected Trip, the North Star strategy guiding Booking.com's product direction and multi-year investment. Booking.com: the product vision for Attractions, for cross-sell and add-ons across travel verticals, and for the whole post-booking experience, from trip planning to managing the booking.

#### The product strategy
What it means: How the product reaches the vision this year: the bets, why each one, how success is measured, and the trade-offs made explicit for the whole product team.
My proof: Booking.com: owned the multi-product experience across cross-sell, add-ons, trip planning and post-booking, and oversaw the white-label Packages platform run in partnership with lastminute.com.

#### Tech architecture and capabilities
What it means: What the technology can do today, where the gaps are, and what to build or buy, so product only plans what can be built and engineering builds what the product needs.
My proof: Booking.com: the product architecture behind Connected Trip, adopted across the whole product community.
> “The collaboration was a fantastic two year journey that had a huge impact on the direction of the company and the clarity of what we built. Dani continues to be a trusted advisor I can go to for vision and direct feedback.”
  Molly Stevens, Chief Product Officer at Amplify.One. We defined Booking.com's three-year vision together.

### Growth that moves again
03 · Growth and profitability
Growth has stalled or costs too much. Supply, go-to-market, new markets or margins aren't keeping up, and money goes into AI with no clear return.
- Scaling supply
- Building the go-to-market
- Expanding internationally
- Improving margins
- Efficiency through AI

#### Scaling supply
What it means: More of the right supply, faster. In a marketplace, supply decides whether a search ends in a sale: go after the long tail competitors ignore, onboard partners in days, and keep the terms good enough that they stay.
My proof: Booking.com Attractions: coverage from 30% to 80%, products from 15k to 100k+, transactions from under 1M to 3M+ a year. Zalora: 4,000+ sellers and 130,000 products live within 12 months; its seller program won Gold for Best Use of Relationship Marketing B2B (Loyalty & Engagement Awards, 2015). Global Fashion Group: 12,000 sellers and 350+ international brands, with onboarding cut from 30 days to 10.

#### Building the go-to-market
What it means: The customers, channels and message that turn a product into steady demand, and the sales, partnership and marketing engine that repeats it.
My proof: Booking.com: Ground Transport launched in 13 cities with top suppliers, including NS Dutch Rail; exclusive partnerships secured with Ticketmaster and Etraveli; partner adoption of the hotel extras platform up 80% year on year.

#### Expanding internationally
What it means: Taking what works to new countries, one market at a time: the order of entry, local supply and demand built together, and a playbook each country can run on its own.
My proof: Global Fashion Group: the marketplace rolled out across 6 companies and 27 countries in under a year, and a global partner program launched in 10 markets. Zalora: the marketplace launched across 8 Southeast Asian markets. Rocket Internet: e-commerce ventures launched across emerging markets.

#### Improving margins
What it means: Margin gains that last because the business works differently, not one-off cuts that hurt service: pricing and mix, cost to serve, supplier terms, and the cash tied up in stock and late payments.
My proof: Global Fashion Group: marketplace performance more than doubled year on year, and 9.8 points of margin gained over two years by moving shipping costs onto suppliers.

#### Efficiency through AI
What it means: More output from the same team, and AI spend with a return you can see. AI is aimed at the processes where it saves the most time and cost, and tokens are spent on work that pays back rather than on experiments that go nowhere. People and AI agents work from one shared company memory, with every decision kept alongside its reason. And people get help to actually change how they work.
My proof: Booking.com: OpenAI-based automation for post-booking customer service, built and deployed, live in production, with structural savings projected. My own AI operating system, built and run daily: one memory of every project and decision, daily and weekly planning, and agents that run recurring work on their own; the same set-up I would put in place inside a company.
> “Dani stays receptive to every idea while still making the tough calls. When it comes to follow-through, decision-making, and removing blockers, there’s no one more dependable.”
  Miranda Slayter, Principal Designer at Booking.com.

### A company that runs without the founder in every decision
04 · Organization design and governance
A strong founder with no leadership team below them, an organization shaped by its history, and key knowledge in a few people's heads.
- Building the leadership team
- Designing the organization
- Decision principles and leadership behaviors
- Governance and systems
- Board and investor reporting

#### Building the leadership team
What it means: The first leadership team beyond the founder: which roles the company needs next, who fills them, how decisions move from the founder to the team, and senior people spending their time leading rather than assembling information.
My proof: Booking.com: led a division of 300+ people across product, engineering, design, commercial and operations.

#### Designing the organization
What it means: An organization shaped on purpose rather than by history. The structure follows the strategy. Every team has a written charter (its purpose, scope and way of working), and every role has a clear owner and mandate. The hiring plan is sequenced to the priorities and the budget, so hiring follows the plan instead of the latest departure.
My proof: Zalora: the marketplace organization designed from zero, a regional team of 10 and 7 country managers each leading about 25 people. Global Fashion Group: a central team of 12 running marketplace operations for the whole group, alongside each company's own team.

#### Decision principles and leadership behaviors
What it means: How leaders are expected to decide and behave: a few principles for who decides what and how disagreements get settled, and the behaviors the company rewards and will not tolerate, so the culture holds as the team grows.
My proof: The teams I have led at Zalora, Global Fashion Group and Booking.com.

#### Governance and systems
What it means: A company that runs without the founder in every decision. A yearly plan learns from last year's bets and sets goals, hiring and budget. Quarterly business reviews check results and reset priorities. Every core process has an owner and a known structure, connected to where the work happens. So nothing depends on one person, nothing is rebuilt from scratch, and every review ends in a decision.
My proof: Global Fashion Group: one B2B platform and one operating playbook, built from Zalora's, run across 6 companies. Booking.com: an €80M annual promotions portfolio across travel verticals, and a budget of about €50M. My advisory work uses the leadership operating system from Claire Hughes Johnson's Scaling People: founding documents, goals and an operating cadence.

#### Board and investor reporting
What it means: One set of numbers, drawn from live data, so leaders review the board pack instead of rebuilding it every quarter, and the board sees the same picture as the team.
My proof: Booking.com: contributed to M&A due diligence for BookingGo. Board adviser to ZYMI, preparing its first investment round.
> “Daniele is an amazing leader – he has a rare combination of excellent problem solving skills and a very strong ability to care for and develop the team.”
  Fridtjof Berge, co-founder of Antler. We set up Global Fashion Group's marketplace division together in 2015.

## How I work with you
- 1 We agree where to start We start from the problem, if it is already clear. If it isn't, we look at the company as a whole: how it makes money, how it runs, who leads it, and where the product is going. We then decide together which of the four problems comes first, and the result we are after. 01 Strategy and transformation 02 Product experience and customer centricity 03 Growth and profitability 04 Organization design and governance
- 2 We build what comes next We work side by side, inside your company. We put in place the operating system I have set up in each area I've led: one mission, the few numbers that matter, the right people. We choose those people together, and we build with them.
- 3 We ensure it keeps growing We measure everything by the result: faster execution, better outcomes for customers, revenue growth, and teams that deliver. We end up with infrastructure that lasts and growth that compounds.

### My promise
I bring calm and clarity when the stakes are high, so the right decisions get made. I'm always honest about what I see, because I care about us succeeding together. I push for the result, so the work shows up in your numbers. I build with your people, so they come out stronger.
